title: Quantum Anchor V1.2.4 — Tesseract Anchor Protocol and Measurement Ledger
description: Experimental protocol for coherent state anchoring on superconducting QPUs, together with the measurement ledger that tests it. The original pulse-level protocol (qiskit.pulse, meas_level=0) was deprecated by IBM in 2024 and removed from production QPUs in February 2025. V1.2 migrates to working APIs and reports evidence grades honestly. MEASURED RESULTS: single-qubit dynamics psi(37ns)=0.331662 under a gamma=0 model on ibm_marrakesh (156Q Heron r2); four independent Bell pairs at 96.75-97.63% per-plane balance on IQM Resonance Garnet 20Q using a virtual Z rotation of 0.4398 rad; Tesseract-V2 inter-plane entangling backbone demonstrating 83.01% global multi-plane coherence on IQM Garnet. NEGATIVE RESULTS, documented in full: the corrected anchor-on (gamma=0.5) and anchor-off (gamma=0) conditions both yield 0% clear on IBM; the virtual rz(phi) gate produces no measurable preservation effect compared to an rz-free Bell control (+0.5 pp, within 95% Wilson confidence intervals). The physical anchor-drive compensation effect is NOT proven by any measurement in this work; pulse-level access required to test it was measured to be unavailable on the account tier used. An earlier positive result is retracted as a circuit tautology. The Tesseract architecture (4 planes x 5 phase realities = 20 pre-realities) is a design proposal whose synchronized selection has NOT been demonstrated: the measured 83.01% figure is global 8-qubit coherence of an entangled hypercube state, not 20-reality selection. TESSERACT-V3 (2026-10-08): a five-phase interferometric hardware sweep (H^8 readout, 5/5 phases, 1024 shots per phase, IQM Garnet 20Q) was completed and is NOISE-DOMINATED. Global coherence measured 0.2-1.4%, with the hardware noise floor above the predicted signal (0.3-3.1%). Goodness-of-fit REJECTS the theoretical cos(8*phi) curve (chi2=30.72, df=4, p<0.0001) and CANNOT REJECT a flat, unmodulated response (chi2=1.98, df=4, p=0.7392). The five phases are therefore NOT statistically distinguishable on this hardware, and the cos(8*phi) modulation is NOT established. The interferometric readout is PROVEN in simulation only, where the V1/V2 Z-basis readout was blind to relative phase.
